name: read-swc-ports-unconnected-of-one-element
description: One component's unconnected ports in one request: the member read of `ports` with `derived: ["unconnected"]`, joined on `element` to the `swc` layer's one row of that component (`where` on `name`), so only that component's own ports answer. The join is an inner join on equal values, so a port of any other component finds no match and has no row; the computed value is the layer read's own, so a connected port has no row either. The same request with `form: "count"` answers the number of those ports, and with `limit` it pages them.

context.summary: The base model, where every port is connected, with two ports that nothing connects: `ExampleSWC`'s require port `rSpare` and the require port `rIdle` of a third component, `UnplacedSWC`, both on `IExample`. So the layer's unconnected ports are two, one of each component, and the join keeps `ExampleSWC`'s.
context.notes: A read takes no scope and writes no audit record.

expected.notes: `UnplacedSWC`'s `rIdle` has no row: the joined read answers `ExampleSWC`'s row alone, and the inner join drops a port with no match. Each row is the port's row, then the match under its alias (`owner`), which carries the component's identity. Without the `join` the same read answers both ports.
